audit.whatIsWrong: The page tracks 'Twofold Hex (Blink)' as one ability in roughly twenty strings. Twofold Hex is Aurora's Q — a curse missile with a recast that drags the curse back — and it is not a blink. The blink is Across the Veil (W). spikes[0] also calls Q a 'double-bolt', and spikes[3] credits Corrosive Charge with shred.
audit.why: Riot's text: Twofold Hex sends a missile that curses, then recasts to draw active curses back. Across the Veil leaps, enters the spirit realm and turns her invisible. Corrosive Charge deals physical damage and slows — no shred, and no percent-health clause either.
audit.corrected: Every tracked-cooldown reference now names Across the Veil, the ability that actually escapes you; Twofold Hex described as the out-and-recast curse; Q described as slow, not shred.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart shows Aurora / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Aurora — five neutral rows and no Urgot row at all, on a lane he wins 55.68% of. The packet's own defect list flags the same contradiction.
audit.why: The prose is more honest than the chart: levels 1-3 are her poke lane, level 6 flips to Urgot on the execute, first item is her window again, and 2+ items is his. Giving her five of seven stages cannot coexist with the win rate.
audit.corrected: Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Skill / Urgot / Skill / Urgot, proposed as one group with the win[N] pairs, ratings and the whys that sit beside them.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere despite the whole page being built around 'commit when her blink is down'.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22s at rank 1 and 700 range; Twofold Hex 9s at 900; Between Worlds 140s at rank 1. Those numbers are what turn 'wait for the window' into a plan.
audit.corrected: 22s, 9s, 900 range and the 140s ult written into the phases, spikes and cooldown breakdown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions Grievous Wounds despite Spirit Abjuration healing her off every spell and attack she lands.
audit.why: Her passive sustain is what makes chip trades worthless in an extended lane; anti-heal timing decides them.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds written into spikes[2] and spikes[3].

notes: 'Twofold Hex (Blink)' welded Aurora's Q onto her W and was used as the tracked cooldown across the whole page. Twofold Hex is the 900-range curse missile; Across the Veil is the 22s blink that actually escapes Disdain, so the tracked-cooldown fields now name Across the Veil. Per the mirror's finding I did not restore any percent-max-health claim for Corrosive Charge — Riot gives it physical damage and a slow only.
